chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah ibn Mihrān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Whoever apprehends a thief and then pardons him, that is for him to do. But when he is brought before the Imam, he cuts him. If the one from whom the theft was made says, 'I gift it to him,' the Imam does not leave him until he cuts him when he has been brought to him. Gifting is only before he is brought to the Imam, and that is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
"and those who guard the limits of Allah"
So when it reaches the Imam, it is not for anyone to leave it aside.

key_terms.أَهَبُ: I give as a gift, meaning I waive my claim by donation
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the lawful authority who implements the hadd
key_terms.الْهِبَةُ: a gift or transfer made by the owner before formal adjudication
key_terms.حُدُودِ اللَّهِ: the divinely prescribed legal limits and punishments
key_terms.سَارِقًا: a thief who has committed theft

ai.seo_question: Can a theft punishment be waived after the case has been brought to the Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the victim of theft may pardon or gift away the claim before the case is formally raised to the Imam. Once the matter reaches the Imam, the legal hadd is no longer to be waived by private pardon. The cited Quranic phrase is invoked to show the obligation of preserving the divinely set limits.
